newsitem.title: UK: Natwest says Q1 trade up in most divisions.
newsitem.headline: Natwest says Q1 trade up in most divisions.

text.p: Britain's National Westminster Bank said on Tuesday that the trading performance of its operations, excluding its NatWest Markets division, had improved in the first quarter of 1997.

NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of NatWest Bank had earlier taken a net charge of 77 million pounds ($125.7 million) against the group's net profits due to losses arising out of mispricing of interest rate options.
Group chairman Lord Alexander reassured shareholders at the annual meeting on Tuesday that losses at its investment banking unit would not affect other businesses of the group.

"These errors were confined to NatWest Markets alone, indeed to one product area within NatWest Markets. And may I stress that we shall not rest until we are certain that we have put matters right and our control systems are stong," Alexander said.
The options losses, which forced its chief executive Martin Owen take a 300,000 stg cut from his annual bonus, is currently being probed into by a team of independent experts.
"...We have asked them to advise us of all areas in our control systems which could be improved," Alexander told shareholders.
Lord Alexander also reiterated the bank's cautious approach towards UK economy, which it had expressed while announcing its results in March.
"Our view have not changed," Alexander said. He said British economy would slow down on the back of an increase in interest rates after years of "good economic progress".
"As a result we are being very careful not to get carried away with over-enthusiasm to lend money," he said.
"It is simply that we are not prepared to loosen our credit. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
